title: Interview heuristic notebook - Oscar Lambert
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable heuristics I used during Oscar's loop. This is deliberately messy — meant for internal handoff and for preserving the mental model I used while evaluating. Use or ignore.

Context: Onsite loop (virtual). Pair-programming on small batching shim, systems design on model caching, behavioral + culture conversation. Candidate came from a mid-size infra team at a startup; listed strong C++ + Python background, recent work on optimizing KV cache microservices.

High-level gut: leaning positive for IC3 (senior runtime engineer) but some execution risk around shipping in a mixed Python/C++ stack and estimating unknowns quickly.

Heuristics I leaned on (definitions):
- Problem decomposition: can they take a vague SLO + describe measurable subproblems? (prefers concrete metrics, e.g., p95 < 120ms for 1k QPS)
- Latency mental model: do they have intuition for token/seq-length scaling and what affects tail latency?
- Tradeoff articulation: can they enumerate tradeoffs (memory vs latency vs throughput) and propose mitigations?
- Ownership appetite: examples of shipping projects end-to-end and handling production incidents.
- Code hygiene under time pressure: write pragmatic, readable code in pair session.
- Communication clarity: can they explain to product/infra folks without jargon.

Observed notes (raw):
- Problem decomposition: good. Broke the caching design into placement, invalidation, backpressure, and telemetry. Mentioned prefix-KV cache explicitly. Gave SLOs and related tradeoffs. Example: suggested soft-fail to smaller model when KV miss volume spikes. (Green)
- Latency mental model: solid intuition for batching penalties vs KV lookup costs. Used example numbers. Slightly fuzzy when I pressed on GPU kernel throughput vs host-to-device transfer — equivocated, admitted gap. (Yellow)
- Tradeoffs: enumerated quantization vs perf, but didn't propose a quantization-aware rollout plan beyond "test & measure". Lacked a concrete rollback/fallback plan for quality regressions post-quant. (Yellow)
- Ownership: concrete examples of incident response; owned a paging rotation and reduced incident MTTR via runbook changes. Strong signal. (Green)
- Code during pair: wrote clear Python; didn't micro-optimize, but produced a testable shim that handled continuous batching + simple KV async lookup. Missed a small race when inflight requests get cancelled — pointed it out after I hinted. (Yellow)
- Communication: clear, asked clarifying Qs. Good listener. (Green)

Micro-scores (1-5, quick):
- decomposition: "5"
- latency-model: "4"
- tradeoffs: "3"
- ownership: "5"
- coding-under-pressure: "4"
- comms: "5"

Total rough score: "26/30" => maps to ~8.5/10 in my head. Recommend consider for IC3; strong on ownership and shipping, minor gaps in low-level perf kernel knowledge and rollback/telemetry plan for risky changes.

Specific red flags and follow-ups:
- Red flag: limited kernel/driver-level experience. If role will require tuning CUDA kernels or contributing to CUDA paths, need follow-up interview or a take-home micro-benchmarking task.
- Red flag: lightweight quantization rollout plan. Ask for a follow-up: "How would you run a canary for a quantized model that sometimes changes tokenization behaviors?" Expecting a plan with prompt set, quality delta thresholds, and automated rollback.

Suggested follow-ups (concrete interview prompts):
1) Deep-dive session on kernel/hardware tradeoffs: give concrete sequence-length vs throughput numbers and ask candidate to pick an approach for 2 different GPU generations.
2) Mini take-home (2-4 hours): rework the pair-session shim to handle cancellation races and add a tiny perf harness (simulate x requests and measure tail). Assess ability to reason about instrumentation.
3) Culture fit: ask them to run a short postmortem sketch on one of their incidents, focusing on learning loops and cross-team comms.

On role and leveling:
- Fit for IC3 (senior runtime engineer): yes, given ownership signals and system-level thinking.
- For IC4 (staff), would need demonstrable low-level perf wins and experience shaping runtime architecture across teams. Not enough evidence today.

Suggested hire recommendation options (pick one):
- Strong hire (IC3): proceed to offer after take-home or kernel follow-up. (my pick)
- Hire-with-conditions: offer with expectation to shadow kernel team for 3 months + training.
- No hire: if you need immediate CUDA/kernel contributor. (only if role differs)

Bias notes / uncertainties (callouts for committee):
- I tend to overweight ownership stories — candidate had good incident examples but we should validate concrete technical depth with the follow-up.
- Candidate is senior at a smaller org; gauge how transferable their context is to our multi-tenant, quantization-forward stack.

Quick ramp sketch if hired (first 90 days):
- Week 1-2: onboarding, infra, and live runbook study; small bug fixes in batching shim.
- Month 1: pair with kernel engineer on a bounded perf task (observe & document bottlenecks).
- Month 2: take ownership of one small feature (e.g., prefix-KV eviction policy or tracer hooks) and ship.
- Month 3: lead a retrospective and propose measurable SLO improvements.

Action items for hiring committee / interviewer owner:
- Diego: run kernel-deep-dive (30-45m) or assign to kernel SME. Link: GH PR above.
- Hiring lead: confirm offer band and whether we require take-home; I recommend take-home focused on race + perf harness.
- Recruiter: ask candidate if they are comfortable with a 2-4 hour take-home and an additional 45m kernel deep-dive.

Quick TL;DR to paste into panel summary: "Strong senior runtime candidate with excellent ownership and systems thinking. Needs a short follow-up on low-level perf/kernel work and a focused take-home to validate race/telemetry practices. Recommend IC3 hire contingent on follow-up."

Notes-to-self (random):
- Oscar's analogy of "cache as lease" was neat — might be worth stealing for a writeup.
- He mentioned an open-source tool he used for async tracing (not sure name). Follow-up question for recruitment: send link and ask candidate to share a short one-pager of a perf win.

End of notes.
